section_1.title: The Counter-Intuitive Hook
section_1.content: Introduce the puzzle: How can two simple blocks colliding on a frictionless surface calculate the digits of pi? Visualize the blocks: a small block (mass m) and a much larger block (Mass M = 100^n * m).
section_1.example: A tiny hamster-sized block slides toward a massive elephant-sized block resting against a wall.

section_2.title: Prerequisite Physics: Conservation Laws
section_2.content: Briefly review Elastic Collisions. Use a split-screen animation showing Conservation of Momentum (mv_i = mv_f + Mv_f) and Conservation of Kinetic Energy (1/2mv^2). Explain why these laws force the blocks to exchange velocity states.
section_2.example: Visualize velocity as a vector arrow that shrinks or grows as energy is transferred during the 'bounce'.

section_3.title: Mapping Collisions to Phase Space
section_3.content: Introduce the 'Phase Space' diagram. Instead of tracking time, track the velocities of the two blocks as coordinates (x, y). The collision path traces a circular arc on a graph. The boundary conditions (wall and origin) force the trajectory to zig-zag.
section_3.example: A laser pointer drawing a circular arc that hits a 'wall' and reflects, acting like a billiard ball in a restricted angle.

section_4.title: The Geometric Connection
section_4.content: Explain that the total number of collisions is proportional to the arc length of the circular segment. As M becomes infinitely larger (100^n), the arc segment length relates directly to the ratio of the circumference to the diameter (pi).
section_4.example: Show an animation where for M=100m, there are 31 collisions; for M=10,000m, there are 314 collisions.

section_5.title: Conclusion and Intuition Check
section_5.content: Summarize how discrete physical events (collisions) map onto continuous geometric constants. Emphasize that pi isn't just about circles, but about the periodic nature of symmetry and conservation.
section_5.example: A final visual of the digit sequence 3-1-4-1-5 appearing on a scoreboard as the blocks bounce, finalizing the link between mechanics and pure math.
